thread:
alexa: hey team, getting paged — sudden spike in 5xx from model-runner pool in us-west-2. starts ~10:12 UTC, error rate ~12% now. sims and production both showing.
incidentbot: INCIDENT CREATED • ID: INC-2026-0423-0923 • Severity: P2 • Pager: alexa • Channel: #incidents
alexa: seeing a mix of OOMs and segfaults in the runner logs. stack traces point to tensor allocator. logs attached below.
jordan: I'm on it. which model variant? small/medium/quantized?
alexa: mostly medium-int8 (m-medium-q8) serving 2k rps. recent deploy? none in last 3h.
priya: tagging infra — could be a kernel regression or driver. opsbot: gpu-driver-alert — driver 525.85.12 installed on 3 nodes today.
sam: grabbing logs from node-578 & node-582. command: `runeadm logs --node node-578 --tail 500`.
li: I see repeated OOM messages in node-578: ```
[FATAL] tensorflow_alloc.cc:345 OutOfMemoryError: failed to allocate 1.2G
backtrace: ...
segfault at 0x7fffa1b0
``` 
maria: client telemetry shows ~40 enterprise calls failing with 502 over last 10m. top-affected routes: /v1/generate and /v1/chat/stream
jordan: quick mitigation idea — enable fallback routing to cpu-quantized model for requests hitting medium-int8. That reduces throughput but should cut 5xx.
alexa: agree. priya, can you flip the fallback policy for us-west-2 to allow fallback immediate? config is behind feature-flag `runtime.fallback.allow_oversubscribe`.
priya: toggling now: `cfg set runtime.fallback.allow_oversubscribe true --env us-west-2` -> applied. pushing policy to routers.
incidentbot: POLICY UPDATE: runtime.fallback.allow_oversubscribe=true (applied by priya)
alexa: traffic planner — start diverting 30% of medium-int8 requests to m-medium-cpu-q4. Use gradual 30->60 if stable.
jordan: doing canary bump: `router scale-route --route medium-int8 --to-model m-medium-cpu-q4 --percent 30 --region us-west-2`.
opsbot: draining node-578 from serving pool for further inspection: `nodectl drain node-578`.
sam: investigating core dump from node-582. `gdb --batch -ex "thread apply all bt full" /usr/bin/runner core.582` gives repeated crash in `kv_cache.cpp:412`.
li: is there a recent change to kv cache eviction logic? last commit 5 days ago (PR #419). but deploys show none for 3h.
maria: started notifying affected customers — two enterprise customers reported timeouts on chat. posting status update to status.redwood.ai -> message queued.
alexa: good. monitoring latency and error rates. initial metric after fallback: error rate dropped to 4% within 4 minutes, p95 latency up from 120ms -> 250ms for routed requests.
priya: infra note — 3 nodes got updated GPU driver this morning by automated batch. rolling back driver on node-582 now.
jordan: rollbacks in-progress: node-582 driver rollback -> SUCCESS. node-578 already drained.
sam: core analysis: memory allocation path on GPU is hitting fragmentation; when combined with medium-int8 kernel it tries a single large contiguous alloc and fails. fallback to cpu variant avoids this.
alexa: short-term mitigation done. next steps: isolate kernel/allocator bug. priya/ops: collect kernel logs, driver versions, and open ticket with vendor if rollback doesn't fully stabilize.
priya: filing vendor ticket with logs and core dump — TICKET-ID: VEND-99321. attaching `/var/log/nvidia-installer.log` and core dump.
li: internal task: revert or patch kv_cache allocator to use split-alloc path. I'll open PR with patch to try smaller chunk allocations. TAGGING: eng-runtime.
maria: status update posted: "We’re seeing elevated errors in us-west-2 affecting a subset of inference requests. Mitigation in place (fallback routing). We’ll post updates every 30m." :bell:
alexa: we need an incident handoff at 11:00 UTC to oncall in europe. sam, can you take first handoff? I'll stay until handover.
sam: I can take handoff. I'll prepare a summary and list of outstanding actions.
jordan: remaining items: 1) confirm no regression on canary traffic, 2) finish driver rollback if any nodes still on broken driver, 3) reproduce alloc with smaller test harness, 4) PR for allocator patch.
priya: rolling verification: node pool error-rate per-node: node-579=1.2%, node-580=0.8%, node-581=0.5%, node-578=drained, node-582=rolled-back=0.3%.
li: started local reproducer against v0.9.3 runtime with medium-int8 and pinned batch size 64. hitting OOM in ~30s. adding guards in reproducer to reduce alloc size.
sam: handoff note (to be used by next oncall): root cause suspected memory fragmentation + driver interaction. Temporary mitigation: fallback routing. Long term: allocator patch + vendor driver analysis. contact list: alexa, jordan, priya, li.
alexa: adding postmortem owners: li (root cause & reproducer), jordan (rollout/playbook update), priya (infra/drivers), sam (customer comms & handoff).
incidentbot: INCIDENT UPDATE • INC-2026-0423-0923 • Status: Mitigated -> P2 -> Ongoing monitoring
maria: posted customer follow-up to affected clients; two customers requested private postmortem support, forwarded to solutions-eng.
sam: handing off now to eu-oncall. alexa, leaving channel in 5.
alexa: thanks all. leaving notes in #postmortems/INC-2026-0423-0923 and will add timeline.
priya: one more note — enabled more aggressive prefix caching to lower memory pressure on inference nodes: `cfg set runtime.caching.prefix_cache_enabled true`.
li: pushed initial PR for allocator change (PR #444). marking as WIP.
jordan: will schedule a canary test across regions tomorrow 03:00 UTC.
sam: acknowledged handoff. monitoring alerts set. I'll escalate to vendor if we see any reappearance.
maria: closing loop with customers: they confirmed degraded but acceptable for now. will keep them updated.
incidentbot: INCIDENT - INC-2026-0423-0923 • CLOSED: No — monitoring continues. next update in 30m."
